inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Look, what we are witnessing right now with the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth support programme workers is a glaring indictment of systemic state exploitation and institutional neglect. These frontline workers had to bravely take to the streets outside the Presidential Palace to confront their precarity and demand basic dignity and legally binding job security guarantees, because they refuse to remain trapped in this vicious cycle of labor exploitation that the ruling class relies upon to maintain the status quo at the expense of the vulnerable. 

Predictably, the government is desperately trying to dodge accountability, claiming they have already delivered on the most significant demands. It is the classic playbook of those in power: trying to silence marginalized workers with hollow, empty promises rather than committing to the deep structural reform that is actually needed. But the working class sees right through these institutional tactics, which is precisely why these workers have announced a 24-hour strike. Total solidarity with these workers who are demanding justice against a system that has failed them!
